criteria.criterion: defaults.toml has a new [[default]] with id bug-evidence for bug, wrong-output and regression requests. Its statement requires that the change names the root cause, shows it from data the job can read (records, code path, a failing case), and shows why the wrong output or metric change follows, before any fix. It says a guess labelled as an estimate does not meet it. Its source cites 20261104-054700-e6js, 20261105-051344-q9fv, 20261105-101121-qw9r and 20261105-205835-hk09. The existing root-cause default is not reworded.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. defaults.toml adds [[default]] id="bug-evidence". Its statement opens "Only for bug, wrong-output, regression or slowdown work: name the root cause from readable data. Before any fix, the change names the root cause, shows it from data the job can read (records, a code path or a failing case) and shows why the wrong output or metric change follows from it; a guess labelled as an estimate does not meet this." Its source cites all four job ids, and all four have introspection records in the evidence snapshot. The diff does not touch the root-cause entry. The athena-data test I ran checks that the root-cause statement is byte-identical to the base text, and it passed.

criteria.criterion: crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs has a step called next to ensure_changelog in build_reading that adds the root-cause-evidence criterion and a bug-evidence defaults_applied entry exactly once for bug, wrong-output, regression and slowdown readings, and nothing for other readings. A Grep for bug-evidence in that file shows it.
criteria.evidence: Grep finds `const BUG_EVIDENCE_ID: &str = "bug-evidence";` at reading.rs:306. In build_reading, `ensure_bug_evidence(&mut reading, request_texts);` comes right after `ensure_changelog(&mut reading);` and before `reading.validate()`. The step returns early unless the capability is change and there is at least one criterion. It triggers in two ways: the reader listed bug-evidence without negating it, or names_bug_work finds a bug word near a fix word in the request, the earlier request or the title. It pushes the criterion and the entry only when each is absent. bug_evidence_step_is_called_beside_ensure_changelog passed.

findings.summary: Five changed files are outside the expected deliverables list: crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs, crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs, docs/system-facts.md, docs/decisions.md and docs/design/context-engineer.md.
findings.evidence: The reading expected the reader budget to live in athena.toml. It actually lives in BudgetSet::budget in lib.rs, so the planned budget raise could only happen there. The other four files follow from that raise. system_facts_budgets_match_computed checks system-facts.md. The pin test quoted the literal 2000. context-engineer.md section 8 requires a decision entry for any budget raise. The CHANGELOG names each of these files, and the critic-accepted planned file list includes them. Judged minor because these are the smallest edits that carry out the budget raise the reading anticipated.

findings.summary: When the reader does not list the default, tier-2 detection is a keyword-proximity heuristic, so some bug requests are missed.
findings.evidence: names_bug_work needs one of bug/bugs/regression(s)/slowdown(s)/wrong-output within two words of a fix word. A request like "fix the crash" or "the total is wrong" triggers only if the reader lists bug-evidence (tier 1). The docs and code comments state this limit. False positives are well controlled: compounds such as bug-evidence, the phrase "regression test" and distant word pairs are excluded and tested. This is acceptable as a backstop, but a reader-side classification field would be more general.

summary: The change does what the retry asked for. defaults.toml gains a bug-evidence default, written for an outside reader: before any fix, the change names the root cause, shows it from data the job can read, shows why the symptom follows, and an estimate does not count. It cites the four rejected jobs and leaves the root-cause default unchanged. In reading.rs, a new step, ensure_bug_evidence, runs in build_reading right after ensure_changelog and before validation. For change readings about bug work it adds the evidence criterion and a bug-evidence entry exactly once. It decides what counts as bug work from the reader listing the default, or from a bug word near a fix word in the request, the earlier request on a retry, or the title. The 13 athena-core tests cover positive and negative cases, retries, negated listings, the empty-criteria refusal and idempotency; with the fix reverted they do not compile. I ran the athena-core, athena-data and athena-context tests and the budget tests, and all passed. The recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed. athena.toml and records/ are untouched. There are two minor findings. First, the reader budget raise had to go in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs, not athena.toml as the reading assumed, which brought in five files outside the deliverables list; all are disclosed and each is needed for the raise. Second, keyword detection only backs up the reader listing the default, and its limits are documented.
